name: Owner inbox page: a private page where the owner reads answers, marks them read, sends his picks, and comments on or moves rows of the feature backlog

title: The owner's inbox page and its feature backlog are missing from the feature list
what: The backlog calls the owner inbox page and the backlog with comments Live. A script that builds this page exists, but the feature list has no row for it, so nothing in this audit checks it. It was not driven here, so whether it works today is unknown.
expected: Every tool the owner uses has a row in the feature list, with its checks.
how_often: every time he opens the page
fix_line: Add the owner inbox page to the feature list and give it a journey

name: Teen accounts (13 to 17): a parent's mobile or email, a one-time code and the parent's I agree before a member under 18 joins a gym

title: Teen accounts were decided for before the public launch, but none exist
what: On 24 Oct the owner decided: 18 and above for the trial, and teen accounts with a parent's OK built before the public launch. A later entry of 14 Nov says the app is live. A search of the member app, the admin app, the server and the database changes found no parent step and no teen flag. Today the app only asks every person to tick that they are 18 or older.
expected: Teen accounts exist before the app is public, or the decision is changed and written down.
who: gym members aged 13 to 17 and their gyms
how_often: every teen who wants to join
fix_line: Owner decides: build teen accounts now, or keep 18 and above and record that

title: The note says the small trial fee is built, but a trial can only be free
what: The owner picked a small trial fee (for example Rs 199 for 7 days), taken off the plan when the person joins, and the note says it was built with the free trial. In the code the trial fee is always zero and the owner's trial card offers only Off, 1, 3 or 7 free days. The fee waits for online joining payments, which are switched off. This is an inside note; no gym is told the fee exists.
expected: The owner can set a trial fee, or the note says the fee is not built yet.
who: gym owners who want a paid trial
fix_line: Correct the note to say the trial fee waits for online joining payments

title: The busy machines tip was promised with a one-tap move, but it only has Not now
what: The owner was told a member would see a line such as Leg day is quieter on Tuesday, with Move it, where one tap moves the routine to the quieter day. The card in the member app shows the line and one button, Not now, which hides it for 30 days. There is no button that moves the routine. This is an inside note; members were not promised the move.
expected: The tip has a Move it button, or the owner knows it is advice only.
who: members of a gym with busy machines on
fix_line: Add a Move it button to the tip, or tell the owner the tip is advice only

title: The backlog still says workouts never go to our server, but a copy does
what: The backlog row Workouts stay on the phone is marked Live and says workouts never go to our server. The same row adds that this changes once the server copy is switched on, and other entries say that happened in late October. In the code, for a member signed in with Google, every saved workout, body weight, measurements and the profile are copied to the server. The row was never updated.
expected: The backlog says plainly that signed-in members' workouts are kept on the server, readable only by them.
who: the owner, and anyone he repeats the line to
how_often: every time the row is read
fix_line: Rewrite the backlog row to say what is copied to the server and for whom

title: The backlog says the signing key is kept only on the owner's PC, but the cloud build holds it too
what: The backlog row Private signing key says the app's signing key is kept only on the owner's PC. The release build signs the app with a key stored as a secret in the code host, and a later entry in the same notes says so. The key is not in the public code, so that half is true; the word only is not.
expected: The row says the key is on the PC and also stored as a private build secret.
how_often: every time the row is read
fix_line: Correct the backlog row to name both places the key is kept
